richText: Auto-configuration provides Spring configuration when stated conditions match.
Conditions can check available classes, existing beans, properties, and the application type.
A library being present does not guarantee that every related feature will be configured. Required properties and other conditions must also match.
Many auto-configured settings can be changed through application properties.
Many auto-configurations back off when you define the corresponding bean yourself. The exact condition depends on the configuration.
Excluding an auto-configuration disables that configuration. It does not remove its library dependency.
Start with --debug to see the condition evaluation report. It shows which configurations matched and which did not.

example.title: Inspect auto-configuration decisions
description: Run a packaged application with debug reporting enabled. Use the actual JAR name produced by the build.
explanation: Read the condition evaluation report in the startup logs.
The report describes configuration conditions. It does not prove that a database or external service is reachable.
